items: ## 8\. Further Study Options After a Master’s in Civil Engineering
After completing a recognised Master’s in Civil Engineering, students may consider additional qualifications or research in areas such as:
PhD in Civil Engineering: Research in infrastructure, structural systems, materials or construction.
Structural Engineering: Advanced analysis and design of buildings, bridges and other structures.
Geotechnical Engineering: Study of soil mechanics, foundations and ground engineering.
Transportation Engineering: Research and planning for roads, transport networks and mobility infrastructure.
Environmental Engineering: Water management, waste treatment and environmental infrastructure.
Construction Project Management: Advanced planning, budgeting, scheduling and project delivery.
These are potential further-study areas, not confirmation that all such programmes are offered in Mauritius. Entry requirements depend on the university and the student’s previous qualification.
## 9\. Career Opportunities After Civil Engineering

A recognised civil engineering master’s may help graduates pursue specialised roles in construction, infrastructure, consultancy and project delivery. Actual eligibility depends on professional recognition, experience and local requirements. A Master’s in Civil Engineering in Mauritius for Indian Students can be a step towards these career directions, depending on the qualification and experience gained.
Potential career paths include:
Structural engineer: Analyses and designs structures such as buildings and bridges.
Civil project engineer: Coordinates technical tasks and project execution.
Construction engineer: Supports construction planning, methods and site operations.
Public works engineer: Works on infrastructure projects and public assets.
Geotechnical engineer: Focuses on foundations, soil conditions and ground stability.
Infrastructure consultant: Provides technical advice on civil engineering projects.
Construction project manager: Coordinates schedules, budgets, resources and project delivery.
Research engineer: Supports studies into construction materials, structural systems and infrastructure performance.
Some positions require professional registration or additional experience. Students should check the relevant engineering registration rules in the country where they plan to work.
## 10\. Documents Required to Study in Mauritius
International applicants should prepare the documents requested by the university. These may include:
Valid passport.
Bachelor’s degree certificate.
Official academic transcripts.
Proof of English and French language proficiency, as applicable.
Completed application form.
Application fee receipt.
CV or résumé, if requested.
Certified translations of academic documents, where required.
Evidence of funds for tuition and living expenses, if requested.
Additional documents needed for admission or immigration.

Because UdM’s course includes some modules in English and others in French, applicants should pay particular attention to the published language conditions and ask the university what evidence it accepts.
## 11\. Frequently Asked Questions
### 1\. Is a Master’s in Civil Engineering available in Mauritius?
Yes. The Université des Mascareignes offers a Master in Civil Engineering with specialisation in Structures and Public Works. It is available part-time to local and international students.
### 2\. How long does the Master in Civil Engineering take?

UdM lists a three-year route for eligible BAC+3 Civil Engineering graduates and a 1.5-year route for eligible BAC+4 graduates entering at Semester 3\. The university must confirm your individual eligibility.
### 3\. What is the tuition fee for Civil Engineering in Mauritius?

UdM currently lists its tuition and registration fees for this programme as to be finalised. The one-off application fee is listed as MUR 700 or US\$25. Contact the university for the current tuition schedule and details about Civil Engineering Fees in Mauritius.
### 4\. Are English and French required for admission?

The published course information states that some modules are taught in English and others in French. Applicants must have passed both languages at high-school or university level, or hold an acceptable language-proficiency certificate. Confirm the documents accepted by UdM before applying.
### 5\. What careers can I pursue after a Master’s in Civil Engineering?

Depending on your specialisation and experience, potential roles include structural engineer, civil project engineer, construction engineer, geotechnical engineer, infrastructure consultant and construction project manager. Professional registration may be necessary for certain positions.
